pointers.heading: When you examine the file size
pointers.text: `SKILL.md` has a maximum of 20,000 bytes.

pointers.heading: When you examine the file size
pointers.text: The glossary, `MEMORY.md`, and `docs/agents/` files

pointers.heading: When the write job makes a SKILL.md or entry-file text
pointers.text: Move text to reference files from a new `SKILL.md` and from new entry-file text.

pointers.heading: When the write job makes a SKILL.md or entry-file text
pointers.text: Write one pointer for each reference file, as "When you put the text in sections and lists" in `plain-language-rules.md` tells you.

pointers.heading: When the edit job changes a SKILL.md or an entry file
pointers.text: Under that heading, write the pointer as "When you put the text in sections and lists" in `plain-language-rules.md` tells you.

pointers.heading: When the file is the glossary, MEMORY.md, or a Rule
pointers.text: For the glossary and `MEMORY.md`, use the format that the project uses.

pointers.heading: When the file is the glossary, MEMORY.md, or a Rule
pointers.text: This skill has no template for the glossary or `MEMORY.md`.

pointers.heading: When the file is the glossary, MEMORY.md, or a Rule
pointers.text: When the project has no glossary, give each term and its definition, as `technical-terms.md` tells you.

pointers.heading: Plain-language rules
pointers.text: They are not applicable to text for persons, for example `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and commit messages.

pointers.heading: Before you use this file
pointers.text: If `SKILL.md` of this skill is not in your context window, read it before you use this file.

pointers.heading: Before you use this file
pointers.text: `SKILL.md` defines the terms, the tiers, and the end-of-run report.

pointers.heading: When you put the text in sections and lists
pointers.text: In reference files, `docs/agents/` files, and files that load in each session, put each rule in a section.

pointers.heading: When you put the text in sections and lists
pointers.text: In the glossary and `MEMORY.md`, copy the format of the entries that the file has.

pointers.heading: When you put the text in sections and lists
pointers.text: Put the pointer to each pointer target in the first file that the agent reads, for example the entry file or the `SKILL.md` file.

pointers.heading: When you select the words and the tone
pointers.text: When you select a word or write a sentence, obey the rules in `ste-rules.md`.

pointers.heading: When you test the text
pointers.text: When you do the self-check or the reader test, read `review.md`.

pointers.heading: When you start a subagent
pointers.text: No platform can make a subagent read-only from a `SKILL.md` file.

pointers.heading: When you start a subagent
pointers.text: The reference files are in the `references/` folder next to the `SKILL.md` file of this skill.

pointers.heading: Before each review round
pointers.text: Run the check script on the full file of each Markdown file of the review target, as "When you run the check script" in `SKILL.md` tells you.

pointers.heading: When you start the reviewers
pointers.text: `review.md`, `loading-rules.md`, `agent-skills-spec.md` for a Skill, and the pointer targets

pointers.heading: When you start the reviewers
pointers.text: `review.md`, `ste-rules.md`, `technical-terms.md`, and the pointer targets

pointers.heading: When you start the reviewers
pointers.text: `review.md`, `plain-language-rules.md`, and the pointer targets

pointers.heading: When you start the reviewers
pointers.text: The glossary and `MEMORY.md` are not pointer targets.

pointers.heading: When you start the reviewers
pointers.text: A reviewer reviews the glossary and `MEMORY.md` only when the job changed them, through the `Changes:` line.

pointers.heading: When you start the reviewers
pointers.text: When you start the reviewers, find the list files in "Terms in this skill" in `SKILL.md`.

pointers.heading: When you start the reviewers
pointers.text: Where `review.md` gives 3 reviewers, 3 reports, or the same `Changes:` line for each reviewer, give no list file to the loading reviewer.

pointers.heading: During and after a review round
pointers.text: Run it as "When you run the check script" in `SKILL.md` tells you.

pointers.heading: After the last review round
pointers.text: Run the check script on the full file of each changed file, as "When you run the check script" in `SKILL.md` tells you.

pointers.heading: After the self-check: the reader test
pointers.text: For example, a pointer "Before you write code about an Order, read `GLOSSARY.md`" is applicable to a task about the code of an Order.

pointers.heading: After the self-check: the reader test
pointers.text: For a Skill, the first file is its `SKILL.md`.

pointers.heading: After the self-check: the reader test
pointers.text: When no entry file changed, the first file is the entry file of the project, for example `AGENTS.md`.

pointers.heading: After the self-check: the reader test
pointers.text: Run the report form for reader reports as "When you run the check script" in `SKILL.md` tells you.

pointers.heading: After the reader test: the output tests and the manual checks
pointers.text: A project often keeps the tests of a Skill in a folder with a `README.md` file, for example `tests/skills/<category>/<name>/`.

pointers.heading: After the reader test: the output tests and the manual checks
pointers.text: Run each test as the `README.md` of the tests tells you.

pointers.heading: After the reader test: the output tests and the manual checks
pointers.text: Then grade each test as that `README.md` tells you.

pointers.heading: When you run a manual check
pointers.text: Make the setup of the check in that copy, as the `README.md` of the tests tells you.

pointers.heading: When no subagent is available
pointers.text: Write it as the Warnings part in `end-of-run-report.md` tells you.

pointers.heading: When a reviewer gives a finding
pointers.text: When a reviewer gives a finding, correct your text, or reject the finding as `references/review.md` tells you.

pointers.heading: When you save a file or run a command in a round
pointers.text: You can save the JSON output of the check script with `>`, as `SKILL.md` shows.

pointers.text: They are not applicable to text for persons, for example `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and commit messages.

pointers.heading: When you select a technical noun
pointers.text: When you select a technical noun, use a noun from the glossary or the base list in `technical-terms.md` (rule 1.8).

pointers.heading: When you select a technical noun
pointers.text: When the glossary and the base list have no noun for an item, do the steps in "When a technical noun is not in the base list or in the glossary" in `technical-terms.md`.

pointers.heading: When you select a technical noun
pointers.text: Write a term in bold only when the glossary or the base list in `technical-terms.md` has it (rule 1.8).

pointers.heading: When you write a sentence
pointers.text: Obey "When a technical noun is not in the base list or in the glossary" in `technical-terms.md` for it.

pointers.heading: When you write a sentence
pointers.text: When you write "rule" in lowercase, read "When you write the word rule" in `technical-terms.md` for the two meanings.

pointers.heading: When you count words
pointers.text: Read references/review.md first.
